why: Protocol section 4's pairing rule, and X17's false-exclusion requirement: BOTH NUMBERS ARE REPORTED OR NEITHER IS. The negative suite alone cannot tell a control that refuses the seventeen adverse cases from one that refuses everything, and a control that refuses everything passes every adverse row. Each fixture here is the registry edit its paired adverse case's BENIGN column implies, and it must PASS validation. A benign fixture that fails is a false exclusion, which is a defect of the same class as a missed adverse case and is reported the same way.
checked_by: tools/run_positive_fixtures.py: declared-but-absent and present-but-undeclared both fail, and a fixture that does NOT pass validation fails
validate_contracts.py: the positive run's own count must equal this one, every declared fixture must have passed, and the declared count must not fall below the floor
floor_why: A literal, for the reason every other floor in this package is a literal: a count derived from the directory it measures is satisfied by the empty directory. Seventeen is one benign case per adverse case of selection-record section 12.5, and dropping one would drop the pairing rule for that row. Lowering this number is a decision and should read like one. RAISED BY R18 (the Step 6 repair of the F2 layer): negative 56 -> 91, positive 17 -> 52. Thirty-five new adverse cases and thirty-five paired benign ones, one per finding the four Step 6 reviews raised against the contracts, plus one pair per guard that had none. F6C-16 measured 14 of 30 guards exercised by a paired fixture; every registered guard has one now, and the count is derived rather than quoted -- `comm -12 <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/negative | sort -u) <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/positive | sort -u) | wc -l`. Lowering either number is still two edits and a written reason. RAISED TO THE COMMITTED COUNT BY THE RC5 REPAIR: positive 53 -> 55 (RC5-01, RC5-03: the allowlist-literal pair and the not-admitted pair) and 55 -> 56 (RC5-02: the pin-coverage pair). R20 (F6A-10): 56 -> 57, the closed-enum membership pair. R21 (F6D-12): 57 -> 58, the seventh-reason pair. R22 (F6D-09): 58 -> 59, the predicate-bearing type pair. R23 (F6C-11): 59 -> 60, the retention-comparison pair. R24 (F6C-10): 60 -> 61, the attempt-ceiling pair. R25 (F6D-09, the wrong_reason repair): 61 -> 62, the predicate-implementation-status pair. The F6D-09 tripwire had to stop firing on the negative-fixture sentinel, because a fixture that adds a predicate must give that predicate a status and was tripping a check about the CONTRACT's classification inside its own scratch tree -- which is what refused r3-lifecycle-status-as-judgment-subject for a reason it was not written for. The pair is what bounds the exclusion: the adverse case gives a real predicate a real second classification and the tripwire must still fire; the benign case gives one the sentinel and it must not. R26 and R27 (F6X-02): negative 101 -> 103, positive 62 -> 64 -- the boundary-kind pair and the contested-refs pair. F6X-02 is the finding two lanes declined on the ground that the enum members would have been invented; `05` section 5 states them now, so the enum is derived and the failure mode moves from `the field admits anything` to `someone adds a ninth member in a diff that reads as a feature`. Both adverse cases are one-line edits to a list, which is why each has a reordering beside it: a control that cannot tell a widening from a reordering is one a contributor routes around. R28 and R29 (F6X-01): negative 103 -> 105, positive 64 -> 66 -- the exclusive-factory resolution pair and the kernel-exemption pair. Nine records declare an exclusive factory and validate_contracts.py resolved NONE of them until this repair, so three declarations naming no existing path had sat green. The second pair exists because the repair introduces an exemption, and an exemption with no adverse fixture is a hole: r29 refuses an invented kernel path and its benign twin accepts a declared one, so the exemption cannot quietly become a prefix rule. R30 (F6A-09): negative 105 -> 106, positive 66 -> 67 -- the alias-key-is-a-value-type pair. The adverse case is the REAL row the review found, restored, because it passed every check in this package for its whole life: the refusal compared alias keys against record names and the key was a registered value type. The benign twin keeps the table addable, which is what it is for.
